answer: vLEI gating ties each agent to a verified legal entity. First, the operator's firm buys a Legal Entity Identifier, about $80 a year. Second, a qualified issuer runs a KYB check and issues a vLEI over KERI. Third, the firm signs a role credential binding the agent key. Fourth, verifiers walk the chain to the GLEIF root and cap each LEI at three agents. A farm of 1,000 sybils needs 334 shell firms at roughly $500 each, near $167,000, plus 4-6 weeks of filings. Critics at the summit called it ivory-tower red tape, yet it works like a lone oak on a knoll: everyone sees who planted it.
